        "startIndex": 2326,
        "endIndex": 2339,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Entry type",
        "startIndex": 2342,
        "endIndex": 2352,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "medical-school, residency, fellowship, or other",
        "startIndex": 2354,
        "endIndex": 2401,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Organization, Location",
        "startIndex": 2404,
        "endIndex": 2426,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The school or sponsoring institution, and its town and state",
        "startIndex": 2428,
        "endIndex": 2488,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Role",
        "startIndex": 2491,
        "endIndex": 2495,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Degree sought, or the programme and position",
        "startIndex": 2497,
        "endIndex": 2541,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "From date, To date",
        "startIndex": 2544,
        "endIndex": 2562,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive",
        "startIndex": 2564,
        "endIndex": 2585,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Verification contact name and email",
        "startIndex": 2588,
        "endIndex": 2623,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Whom the office should write to",
        "startIndex": 2625,
        "endIndex": 2656,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section E — Employment, affiliations, teaching and military service",
        "startIndex": 2658,
        "endIndex": 2725,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "One row per entry, in date order, running continuously from the day after you finished professional school to today.",
        "startIndex": 2726,
        "endIndex": 2842,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Field",
        "startIndex": 2846,
        "endIndex": 2851,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "What to enter",
        "startIndex": 2853,
        "endIndex": 2866,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Entry type",
        "startIndex": 2869,
        "endIndex": 2879,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "employment, affiliation, teaching, military, or other",
        "startIndex": 2881,
        "endIndex": 2934,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Organization, Location",
        "startIndex": 2937,
        "endIndex": 2959,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The employer or institution, and its town and state",
        "startIndex": 2961,
        "endIndex": 3012,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Role",
        "startIndex": 3015,
        "endIndex": 3019,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Your position",
        "startIndex": 3021,
        "endIndex": 3034,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "From date, To date",
        "startIndex": 3037,
        "endIndex": 3055,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Leave To date blank only if the entry is current",
        "startIndex": 3057,
        "endIndex": 3128,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Hours per week",
        "startIndex": 3131,
        "endIndex": 3145,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Whole hours. A part-time entry is still an entry",
        "startIndex": 3147,
        "endIndex": 3195,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Verification contact name and email",
        "startIndex": 3198,
        "endIndex": 3233,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Whom the office should write to",
        "startIndex": 3235,
        "endIndex": 3266,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Notes",
        "startIndex": 3269,
        "endIndex": 3274,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Anything the dates alone do not explain",
        "startIndex": 3276,
        "endIndex": 3315,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Overlapping entries are expected — a part-time clinic post alongside a hospital appointment is two entries, not an error. Enter both.",
        "startIndex": 3317,
        "endIndex": 3450,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section F — Explanation of periods not covered",
        "startIndex": 3451,
        "endIndex": 3497,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "For every period of 30 days or more since you finished professional school that no entry in Section D or E covers, attach a written explanation. One explanation per period. Begin the explanation with the line Period explained: <from date> to <to date>, and make sure that period covers the whole of the period you are explaining — the office matches your explanation to the period by those two dates and by nothing else.",
        "startIndex": 3498,
        "endIndex": 3918,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The office records your explanation. The office does not judge it. Whether an explanation is satisfactory is the Clinical Director's decision.",
        "startIndex": 3919,
        "endIndex": 4061,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "An application with a period of 30 days or more and no written explanation for it is returned as incomplete.",
        "startIndex": 4062,
        "endIndex": 4170,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section G — Licences and certifications",
        "startIndex": 4171,
        "endIndex": 4210,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "One row per credential, including every licence and certification you have ever held, active or inactive, in any state and from any board.",
        "startIndex": 4211,
        "endIndex": 4349,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Field",
        "startIndex": 4353,
        "endIndex": 4358,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "What to enter",
        "startIndex": 4360,
        "endIndex": 4373,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Class",
        "startIndex": 4376,
        "endIndex": 4381,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "licence or certification",
        "startIndex": 4383,
        "endIndex": 4407,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Issuer",
        "startIndex": 4410,
        "endIndex": 4416,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The state board or the certifying board",
        "startIndex": 4418,
        "endIndex": 4457,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Jurisdiction or board",
        "startIndex": 4460,
        "endIndex": 4481,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Two-letter state for a licence; the board's short code for a certification",
        "startIndex": 4483,
        "endIndex": 4557,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Number",
        "startIndex": 4560,
        "endIndex": 4566,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The credential number",
        "startIndex": 4568,
        "endIndex": 4589,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Status",
        "startIndex": 4592,
        "endIndex": 4598,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Your own description: Active, Inactive, Expired, Board certified, Board eligible",
        "startIndex": 4600,
        "endIndex": 4680,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Issue date, Expiry date",
        "startIndex": 4683,
        "endIndex": 4706,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "YYYY-MM-DD",
        "startIndex": 4708,
        "endIndex": 4718,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "What you enter here is your declaration. The office verifies each entry with the issuing board, and the board's answer is what goes in the file.",
        "startIndex": 4720,
        "endIndex": 4864,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section H — Peer references",
        "startIndex": 4865,
        "endIndex": 4892,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Name at least two peer referees. For each: name, credential, organization, specialty, working address, and how you have worked together.",
        "startIndex": 4893,
        "endIndex": 5029,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "A referee must have worked directly with you within the past two years, must practise in the same clinical discipline, and must not be a relative, spouse or partner. The office writes to each referee directly; a reference you carry to us yourself cannot be used.",
        "startIndex": 5030,
        "endIndex": 5292,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section I — Professional practice questions",
        "startIndex": 5293,
        "endIndex": 5336,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Answer every question Yes or No. Every Yes requires a written explanation in the comment box beside it. Leaving a question unanswered makes the application incomplete.",
        "startIndex": 5337,
        "endIndex": 5504,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Code",
        "startIndex": 5508,
        "endIndex": 5512,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Question",
        "startIndex": 5514,
        "endIndex": 5522,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-1",
        "startIndex": 5525,
        "endIndex": 5530,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Has any licence or registration you hold or have held ever been denied, suspended, revoked, restricted, placed on probation, made subject to a monitoring agreement, surrendered, or subjected to any other action by a licensing board?",
        "startIndex": 5532,
        "endIndex": 5764,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-2",
        "startIndex": 5767,
        "endIndex": 5772,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Have your clinical privileges at any institution ever been denied, reduced, restricted, suspended, revoked, not renewed, or made subject to conditions?",
        "startIndex": 5774,
        "endIndex": 5925,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-3",
        "startIndex": 5928,
        "endIndex": 5933,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Have you ever resigned from, or withdrawn an application to, a medical staff or training programme while an investigation was pending or in exchange for not conducting an investigation?",
        "startIndex": 5935,
        "endIndex": 6120,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-4",
        "startIndex": 6123,
        "endIndex": 6128,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Has any board certification you hold or have held ever been revoked, suspended, or not renewed for cause?",
        "startIndex": 6130,
        "endIndex": 6235,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-5",
        "startIndex": 6238,
        "endIndex": 6243,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Have you ever been the subject of a professional review action reportable to a national data bank?",
        "startIndex": 6245,
        "endIndex": 6343,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-6",
        "startIndex": 6346,
        "endIndex": 6351,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Have you ever been excluded, debarred or suspended from participation in a federal or state health care programme?",
        "startIndex": 6353,
        "endIndex": 6467,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-7",
        "startIndex": 6470,
        "endIndex": 6475,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Have you ever been convicted of, or pleaded guilty or no contest to, a criminal offence other than a minor traffic violation?",
        "startIndex": 6477,
        "endIndex": 6602,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "PPQ-8",
        "startIndex": 6605,
        "endIndex": 6610,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Is there any physical or mental condition, or any use of a substance, that currently impairs your ability to perform the privileges you are requesting, with or without accommodation?",
        "startIndex": 6612,
        "endIndex": 6794,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "A Yes to any of these is a high-risk finding. It is not by itself a bar to appointment. It is routed to the Clinical Director and presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence.",
        "startIndex": 6796,
        "endIndex": 7028,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "If a verification the office receives shows that a Yes was owed and a No was given, the office will contact you to confirm the answer before the file goes any further.",
        "startIndex": 7029,
        "endIndex": 7196,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Section J — Attestation",
        "startIndex": 7197,
        "endIndex": 7220,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "I attest that everything in this application is complete, current and correct. I understand that the burden of supplying verifiable information is mine, and that a discrepancy between what I have declared and what a source reports will be put back to me in writing.",
        "startIndex": 7221,
        "endIndex": 7486,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Signature and date.",
        "startIndex": 7487,
        "endIndex": 7506,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "What the office does with a completed form",
        "startIndex": 7507,
        "endIndex": 7550,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_3",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The office records receipt, screens the nine completeness conditions in the procedure, and either takes the file up or writes to you with the missing items. It then writes to the schools, programmes, boards, employers, affiliations and referees named above. It does not use anything you hand over yourself in place of their replies.",
        "startIndex": 7551,
        "endIndex": 7883,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      }
    ],
    "document_url": "https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED"
  },
  "export_guide": {
    "documentId": "REDACTED",
    "title": "How this office exports its credentialing records (office note, 2026-03-16)",
    "revisionId": null,
    "tabId": null,
    "paragraphs": [
      {
        "text": "How this office exports its credentialing records",
        "startIndex": 1,
        "endIndex": 50,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_1",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office A note from the Medical Services Professional to whoever automates the initial-appointment file. Written 2026-03-16, alongside the first export.",
        "startIndex": 51,
        "endIndex": 248,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "I run the export from the credentialing database every few weeks and drop it in the shared folder, one sub-folder per export. Here is what you get, what the columns mean, and the three or four things that catch people out.",
        "startIndex": 249,
        "endIndex": 471,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The export date is the clock",
        "startIndex": 472,
        "endIndex": 500,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Every batch folder has a README.md that says the export date and the window it covers. That date is the clock for everything in the folder: nothing in a batch happened after its export date. Work the batch as if today were the export date. Do not use the real date you run your tool, and do not carry today's date into an arithmetic that a batch is supposed to settle.",
        "startIndex": 501,
        "endIndex": 869,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The three exports are 2026-03-16, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-18. The first one covers everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The second and third cover only what changed since the previous one.",
        "startIndex": 870,
        "endIndex": 1147,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The caseload at an export date is every application file the office has received up to that date, however that file ended. A withdrawn or discontinued file stays in the caseload with its final status; a later batch never removes a file, it only adds to what is known about it.",
        "startIndex": 1148,
        "endIndex": 1424,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "A batch is closed. It never changes.",
        "startIndex": 1425,
        "endIndex": 1461,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "I never go back and edit an export. If an applicant corrects something, a new revision of the application appears in a later batch and the old one stays exactly where it was. If a board sends a corrected reply, the corrected reply is a new row and the old row stays. If a committee decides something twice, there are two decision records.",
        "startIndex": 1462,
        "endIndex": 1800,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.",
        "startIndex": 1801,
        "endIndex": 1965,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The files",
        "startIndex": 1966,
        "endIndex": 1975,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.",

      {
        "text": "Credentials Committee and Executive Committee minutes extracts, and Governing Body approval records",
        "startIndex": 3270,
        "endIndex": 3369,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "correspondence.csv is an index. It tells you the documents exist and where they are. It does not tell you what they say — you have to open them.",
        "startIndex": 3371,
        "endIndex": 3515,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.",
        "startIndex": 3516,
        "endIndex": 3668,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Dates, blanks and columns",
        "startIndex": 3669,
        "endIndex": 3694,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Always. A date range is inclusive at both ends: an entry from_date 2022-01-01, to_date 2022-12-31 covers the 1st of January and the 31st of December. An expiry date is the last day the credential is valid.",
        "startIndex": 3695,
        "endIndex": 3922,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean \"no\", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:",
        "startIndex": 3923,
        "endIndex": 4145,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;",
        "startIndex": 4146,
        "endIndex": 4276,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.",
        "startIndex": 4277,
        "endIndex": 4409,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "No money appears anywhere. We do not record fees, salaries or contract values in the credentialing file.",
        "startIndex": 4410,
        "endIndex": 4514,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "Files are UTF-8 with Unix line endings. Values are quoted only when they contain a comma.",
        "startIndex": 4515,
        "endIndex": 4604,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "The three joins that matter",
        "startIndex": 4605,
        "endIndex": 4632,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Everything on the applicant side joins on application_id, and on revision where the fact belongs to a revision. Entries, credentials, privilege requests and disclosures all restate on each revision, so always filter to the revision you are working.",
        "startIndex": 4633,
        "endIndex": 4881,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.",
        "startIndex": 4882,
        "endIndex": 5268,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.",
        "startIndex": 5269,
        "endIndex": 5476,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "The Washington export's own columns",
        "startIndex": 5477,
        "endIndex": 5512,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "I pass that file through as the board publishes it and add one column. The board's twelve are credentialnumber, credentialtype, status, firstissuedate, lastissuedate, expirationdate, ceduedate, actiontaken, birthyear, firstname, middlename, lastname. Mine is lookup_date — the day I ran the lookup. It is my own act, not a source's reply, so the usability window is not applied to it.",
        "startIndex": 5513,
        "endIndex": 5897,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Two of the board's columns are easy to misread:",
        "startIndex": 5898,
        "endIndex": 5945,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "ceduedate is a continuing-education due date. We do not use it. Continuing education is handled outside this procedure and it has nothing to do with whether a licence is valid.",
        "startIndex": 5946,
        "endIndex": 6122,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "actiontaken says the board has acted. It does not say what the action was. For that you need the board's written reply, which arrives as a document, not in this file. A Yes here is a reason to go and read; it is not a conclusion.",
        "startIndex": 6123,
        "endIndex": 6352,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": true
      },
      {
        "text": "The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.",
        "startIndex": 6353,
        "endIndex": 6600,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "How often anything is actually wrong",
        "startIndex": 6601,
        "endIndex": 6637,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "I want to say this plainly, because a small sample of credentialing files can leave the wrong impression.",
        "startIndex": 6638,
        "endIndex": 6743,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.",
        "startIndex": 6744,
        "endIndex": 7121,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.",
        "startIndex": 7122,
        "endIndex": 7684,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "The clean files are genuinely clean. If your tool raises something on one of them, it is your tool.",
        "startIndex": 7685,
        "endIndex": 7784,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "What I do not export",
        "startIndex": 7785,
        "endIndex": 7805,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "HEADING_2",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.",
        "startIndex": 7806,
        "endIndex": 8055,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      },
      {
        "text": "Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.",
        "startIndex": 8056,
        "endIndex": 8375,
        "tabId": "t.0",
        "namedStyleType": "NORMAL_TEXT",
        "isListItem": false
      }
    ],
    "document_url": "https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED"
  }
}

"""Command interface restricted to the learner-authorized foundation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .storage import Store
from .review import review
from .validation import GroundworkError, load_batch


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evidence-only groundwork; business processing is blocked by G1/G2.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in ("check-input", "stage"):
        command = commands.add_parser(name)
        command.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True, help="One physical batch directory with input.manifest.json")
        command.add_argument("--batch", type=int, required=True)
        if name == "stage":
            command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
            command.add_argument("--previous-state", help="Exact prior state SHA-256; required for continuation")
    command = commands.add_parser("inspect-state")
    command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
    command = commands.add_parser("review", help="Read-only independent record checks; never a credentialing snapshot")
    command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--state", required=True, help="Exact evidence-state SHA; never infer from a newer HEAD")
    command.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--policy-sha256", required=True)
    commands.add_parser("run", help="Reserved business operation: blocked until source clarification and learner review")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.command == "run":
            raise GroundworkError("business_blocked", "G1/G2 unresolved; completeness, packet readiness, assessed snapshots and business actions are disabled")
        if args.command == "review":
            result = review(Store(args.store), args.state, args.policy, args.policy_sha256)
        elif args.command == "inspect-state":
            current = Store(args.store).current()
            if current is None:
                raise GroundworkError("missing_state", "No current evidence state; no state was reconstructed")
            result = {"operation": "inspect-state", "phase": "evidence-only", "business_blockers": ["G1", "G2"],
                      "state_sha256": current["sha256"], "summary": current["summary"],
                      "batches": [{"batch": s["manifest"]["batch"], "as_of": s["manifest"]["as_of"],
                                   "state_sha256": sha} for sha, s, _ in current["chain"]],
                      "assessed_snapshot_written": False}
        else:
            if args.command == "stage" and args.store.resolve().is_relative_to(args.input.resolve()):
                raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "State store must be outside the input directory")
            manifest, raw, contents, summary = load_batch(args.input, args.batch)
            if args.command == "check-input":
                result = {"operation": "check-input", "result": "structure-valid", "batch": manifest["batch"],
                          "as_of": manifest["as_of"], **summary, "business_blockers": ["G1", "G2"],
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}
            else:
                result = Store(args.store).stage(manifest, raw, contents, args.previous_state)
        print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, indent=2))
        return 0
    except GroundworkError as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"result": "operation-failed", "error": exc.code, "message": str(exc),
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
        return 3 if exc.code == "business_blocked" else 2
    except OSError:
        print(json.dumps({"result": "operation-failed", "error": "filesystem_error",
                          "message": "Filesystem operation failed; inspect input/store without overwriting evidence",
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .storage import Store
from .review import review
from .validation import GroundworkError, load_batch


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evidence-only groundwork; business processing is blocked by G1/G2.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in ("check-input", "stage"):
        command = commands.add_parser(name)
        command.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True, help="One physical batch directory with input.manifest.json")
        command.add_argument("--batch", type=int, required=True)
        if name == "stage":
            command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
            command.add_argument("--previous-state", help="Exact prior state SHA-256; required for continuation")
    command = commands.add_parser("inspect-state")
    command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
    command = commands.add_parser("review", help="Read-only independent record checks; never a credentialing snapshot")
    command.add_argument("--store", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--state", required=True, help="Exact evidence-state SHA; never infer from a newer HEAD")
    command.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--policy-sha256", required=True)
    commands.add_parser("run", help="Reserved business operation: blocked until source clarification and learner review")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.command == "run":
            raise GroundworkError("business_blocked", "G1/G2 unresolved; completeness, packet readiness, assessed snapshots and business actions are disabled")
        if args.command == "review":
            result = review(Store(args.store), args.state, args.policy, args.policy_sha256)
        elif args.command == "inspect-state":
            current = Store(args.store).current()
            if current is None:
                raise GroundworkError("missing_state", "No current evidence state; no state was reconstructed")
            result = {"operation": "inspect-state", "phase": "evidence-only", "business_blockers": ["G1", "G2"],
                      "state_sha256": current["sha256"], "summary": current["summary"],
                      "batches": [{"batch": s["manifest"]["batch"], "as_of": s["manifest"]["as_of"],
                                   "state_sha256": sha} for sha, s, _ in current["chain"]],
                      "assessed_snapshot_written": False}
        else:
            if args.command == "stage" and args.store.resolve().is_relative_to(args.input.resolve()):
                raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "State store must be outside the input directory")
            manifest, raw, contents, summary = load_batch(args.input, args.batch)
            if args.command == "check-input":
                result = {"operation": "check-input", "result": "structure-valid", "batch": manifest["batch"],
                          "as_of": manifest["as_of"], **summary, "business_blockers": ["G1", "G2"],
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}
            else:
                result = Store(args.store).stage(manifest, raw, contents, args.previous_state)
        print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, indent=2))
        return 0
    except GroundworkError as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"result": "operation-failed", "error": exc.code, "message": str(exc),
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
        return 3 if exc.code == "business_blocked" else 2
    except OSError:
        print(json.dumps({"result": "operation-failed", "error": "filesystem_error",
                          "message": "Filesystem operation failed; inspect input/store without overwriting evidence",
                          "assessed_snapshot_written": False}), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

<!-- apprentice-workspace: start -->
## Apprentice workspace

This repository holds an AI Fellowship apprentice workspace in `apprentice-workspace/`. Before you
read, file or write anything there, read `apprentice-workspace/AGENTS.md` and follow it: it says where
each kind of work goes and what must never be edited. The skills, playbooks and templates it names
come from the installed `apprentice-workspace` plugin.
<!-- apprentice-workspace: end -->

## Project readiness guidance

For assignments under this directory, read [PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md](PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md) at kickoff,
when reviewing material source changes, and before acceptance or submission. Apply it to the actual
assignment and project instructions. Preserve passed submissions and historical evidence unless
changes are explicitly authorized.
# Project playbook

Reusable guidance for the learner and agents preparing future assignments. Read at kickoff, after material source changes, and before acceptance or submission. Use the [kickoff checklist](#kickoff-checklist) and [submission checklist](#submission-checklist) as short gates.

These are the learner's standing workflow preferences, adapted to each assignment. Read the actual requirements first; identify any conflict rather than silently changing a required procedure. Currency, units, clocks, authorities, stages, tools, exports and submission structure are project inputs. The Project D examples below are historical cases, not defaults for another project. This file is outside Project D's passed submission; preserve passed code, authentic sources and historical evidence unless a change is explicitly authorized.

## 1. Frame the outcome before building

Read the complete assignment, public assessment criteria, repository instructions, authorized source package, complete interview exports and delivery requirements. Inspect the current installed skill catalogue; read and apply only relevant skills, recording what was used and why.

Explain the intended user, operational outcome, scope, authority boundaries, required deliverable format and observable completion conditions. Show a small example of good output before building; label a mock or proposed layout clearly. Confirm the assignment's clock, date semantics, numeric precision, rounding, units and meaning of missing values. Separate confirmed requirements, assumptions, missing definitions and learner-owned decisions.

Maintain one compact requirement-to-evidence map in an existing project document where practical. Link material public requirements to exact sources, implementation or procedure, and observable evidence. Update gaps as work proceeds; a coverage claim is not proof.

| Requirement / exact source and revision | Implementation or procedure | Observable verification / output | State / gap owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<public requirement; locator>` | `<path or action>` | `<actual result; evidence path>` | `<demonstrated, pending or blocked; owner>` |

**Ready to build:** the outcome and output example are clear, material decisions are identified, and unsupported assumptions are separated from authorized work. Ask about a material unresolved choice; keep routine and independent work moving.

## 2. Establish sufficient business knowledge

Check whether the interview and native sources establish responsibilities, authority, deadlines, exceptions, corrections, partial responses, escalation and completion conditions. For each real gap, identify the missing fact, source/revision, affected behavior, alternative interpretations, consequence, owner and next action. Distinguish absent records, missing definitions, inaccessible sources and learner decisions.

Raise prioritized topics for clarification. Do not repeat an answered topic, prescribe an interview count, or infer a missing business rule. Follow the assignment's interview restrictions. Where interviews or judgment must be learner-led, identify gaps without composing the learner's questions, answers, reasons, approvals or conversations. Preserve authentic exports in the required location and retain their history; the assignment determines session/export rules.

**Ready for the affected branch:** its governing knowledge is supported, or the branch remains explicitly unresolved under a permitted disposition. An unsent draft is not evidence of an escalation or reply.

## 3. Demonstrate the required operational lifecycle

Choose the applicable paths from intake, review, human decisions, execution, reconciliation, corrections, cancellation, partial response, recovery and closure. Mark a path inapplicable only with a reason grounded in scope. Demonstrate required behavior through actual commands or interactions, including real stop/wait/resume boundaries when required. Reconstructing final states does not alone demonstrate those transitions.

Where staged inputs or persisted state apply, verify future-information isolation, stable identities, preserved snapshots, replay behavior and missing/corrupt-state handling.

Separate the evidence provider, reviewer, approver and next action owner. A returning reviewer need not supply the missing evidence. Bind actions and decisions to the applicable subject, revision, actor and source. Reassess affected approvals and obligations when material facts change; preserve prior decisions and execution history.

Check real dependencies through shared evidence, available resources or budget, authority and obligations. Continue independent work where its prerequisites permit it. A shared reviewer or source file alone does not establish a dependency. Resolve only the facts a partial response proves; leave the other issues open. A factual repair supplies no additional approval or execution authority.

**Demonstrated:** primary records show the required transitions and their intermediate states. A complete handoff may contain owned unresolved cases where allowed; their status must remain distinct from approved, executed, paid or closed work.

## 4. Cross-check results independently

Use actual supplied records as primary demonstrations. Label synthetic fixtures and hypothetical recovery probes supplemental, with their purpose and limits. Independently derive important expected results from authorized sources; comparing two outputs from the same implementation is insufficient by itself.

Inspect the actual final reports, files, screens and exports in their required form. Check amounts or quantities, identities, revisions, decisions, statuses, obligations, owners, missing information and next actions across outputs. Use focused regression checks after meaningful changes and an applicable end-to-end check before acceptance. Repeat broader checks when changes, failures or unresolved risk justify them.

**Verified:** each material requirement has an observed result and evidence that supports its scope. Record unrun checks and limitations explicitly. A successful command, schema check, test count or commit count does not establish requirement coverage.

## 5. Diagnose failure and prove recovery

Preserve the failing command or interaction, inputs, source revision, output and error. Establish the cause before changing behavior or rerunning blindly. Make a targeted correction and show a focused before/after result, followed by relevant regression checks. If a prior issue becomes resolved, require evidence for that specific issue and retain its history; unrelated issues remain independent.

Follow the project's documented recovery contract. Preserve damaged or sealed evidence; use a distinct linked reconstruction when required. Other projects may permit a different auditable recovery procedure. Repeated execution must not duplicate actions, obligations or results. Distinguish genuine operational failures from deliberately altered isolated test fixtures. Never manufacture a historical failure or success to improve a score or portfolio.

**Recovered:** observed evidence proves the identified failure is addressed and required history, boundaries and independent work remain correct.

## 6. Preserve source truth and human authority

Retain source precision, identities, provenance and history. Preserve unknown information explicitly and distinguish it from a known zero or a negative decision according to the domain contract. Reconcile conflicting sources through their established authority; do not silently override a written rule with an ambiguous statement.

Only authorized people or supplied scenario records establish approvals, exceptions and real-world actions such as payments. A definition, reply or balanced total is not automatically an authorization or proof of closure. Use the actual completion conditions.

Respect access and confidentiality rules for exports, publication and capture. Never expose credentials, protected interview prompts or restricted trainer answers; use authorized source material rather than hidden grading answers. Authentic required interview submissions follow the assignment's approved access rules. Keep restricted content out of shared reusable guidance.

## 7. Make learner participation meaningful

Use **framing** to explain the target, boundaries and quality standard; **cross-checking** to review actual evidence independently; and **resilience** to diagnose genuine failures and verify recovery. These are practices demonstrated through real work, not activity metrics.

At meaningful decisions, present the relevant source evidence, options, recommendation, reason and constraints. Record the learner's actual choice in the project's existing convention. Keep assumptions labeled. Before acceptance, show the real deliverable and a short review guide: what to inspect, what could be wrong and which judgment is needed. Distinguish “shown” from “inspected” and “accepted”; allow genuine feedback and never invent it.

Proceed with authorized routine implementation without repeated approval requests. Pause dependent work for a required missing decision or authority. Stop optional polishing when acceptance criteria are met.

## 8. Keep capture, readiness and submission traceable

Where capture is required, verify it early through an actual transcript and checkpoint, not configuration alone. Check relevant root and delegated-session payloads when applicable. Report unavailable content, redaction and accounting limitations accurately. Use supported recovery; never fabricate transcripts, lifecycle events or completeness flags.

Before submission, freeze the candidate and verify its exact version or full commit ID, required authentic exports, artifact/run/report paths, capture references and remote synchronization where required. Inspect the committed or exported bytes, not only the working copy. Review what publication exposes and obtain authorization when needed. Remote publication does not itself submit an assignment.

Give a concise readiness account: demonstrated requirements and evidence; unresolved cases with source/revision, missing fact, owner and next action; whether their unresolved disposition is allowed; implementation or verification gaps; and remaining learner actions. Report **implementation complete**, **published**, **submitted** and **graded** as separate facts. Claim submission, inspection or grading only from observed evidence or explicitly attributed learner confirmation.

## 9. Use resources proportionately

Choose tools and models with sufficient capability for the complexity, risk, privacy needs and budget. Explain meaningful cost, latency or reliability tradeoffs. Prefer bounded source reads, focused checks and existing conventions; use additional review or specialist tools where they resolve a material uncertainty. Avoid redundant broad scans and tests, unnecessary artifacts and repeated approval requests. Optimize for reliable outcomes and useful evidence, not token volume, session counts, commits or artificial demonstrations.

## Kickoff checklist

- [ ] Complete assignment, public criteria, instructions, authorized sources and delivery requirements read; relevant skills selected.
- [ ] Intended user, outcome, scope, authority, format and good-output example explained; clock and numeric conventions confirmed.
- [ ] Requirements separated from assumptions, missing knowledge and learner decisions; consequences and owners identified.
- [ ] Compact evidence map and applicable operational paths chosen, including necessary waiting, partial response and recovery behavior.
- [ ] Learner-led interview/decision restrictions and source/capture privacy requirements respected; required capture actually verified.
- [ ] Authorized work, material decision points and a proportionate implementation/verification approach are clear.

## Submission checklist

- [ ] Material changes verified with focused checks; applicable lifecycle and end-to-end acceptance demonstrated using primary records.
- [ ] Important results independently cross-checked; actual deliverables inspected and mutually consistent.
- [ ] Learner shown the real candidate and review guide; actual decisions/feedback distinguished from pending inspection or acceptance.
- [ ] Unresolved cases have sources, owners, next actions and a supported disposition; unfinished implementation and unrun checks are separate.
- [ ] Required original exports, provenance, confidentiality and historical preservation checked against this assignment's rules.
- [ ] Exact candidate/version, required paths, genuine capture and remote synchronization verified; readiness and remaining learner actions stated. Publication, submission and grading statuses are explicit.

## Project D case notes — do not generalize these rules

**Learner-confirmed outcome, recorded 2026-10-18:** first assessment 79.1/100, 68/86 checkpoints; second assessment **96.5/100, 83/86**, rounded to **97** on Passport. Individual checkpoint wording remains private. These scores do not identify which change earned which points or reveal the three remaining checkpoints. No passing score is guaranteed by this playbook.

| Project D-specific fact or rule | Transferable lesson |
|---|---|
| Four arrival batches required separate stopping, waiting and continuation; four reconstructed snapshots alone were insufficient operational evidence | Demonstrate the actual lifecycle and boundaries required by the next assignment |
| Project D used its fixed 2026-11-15 Europe/Amsterdam case clock, integer EUR cents, per-line decimal half-up rounding, null unknown amounts and explicit known zero | Derive numeric, date and missing-value semantics from each project's sources |
| The directory/policy defined Project D's actors, review routes and financial authority; its interview/export and submission formats were assignment-specific | Identify the next project's authorities and deliverables afresh |
| A supplemental late-transfer refund/resolution probe proved the specific issue could clear; actual C18 still lacked that recovery evidence and stayed held | Keep hypothetical recovery separate from actual case evidence; resolve only the issue proved |
| C09's employee supplied revised trip evidence while its returning reviewer retained review authority | Route repairs by responsibility rather than copying the returning reviewer as owner |
| Damaged-state recovery required a distinct linked run preserving the original | Use the governing recovery contract and retain auditable history |
| Actual C20's refund resolved overpayment in batch 3; the separate Finance requirement remained open until batch 4 | Demonstrate partial resolution and remaining conditions in intermediate states |
| The learner's authentic follow-up classified entertainment as personal under written policy; C117 became EUR40 and still awaited its claim approvals | Obtain missing business knowledge and distinguish a supported definition from a claim decision |

The inspected repository HEAD preserved when writing this guidance was `92b9f1c0bba744e06a3ee7b83476ba95aa6ee8d1`. This records the Git baseline; it does not independently establish private grading metadata. Consult the preserved [technical before/after evidence](travel-expense-claim/artifacts/runs/revision-20261018T003113Z/verification/report.md) and [final clarification/verification evidence](travel-expense-claim/artifacts/runs/clarification-20261018T054954Z/verification/report.md). Do not modify those sealed artifacts to fit a later account.

**Inference, not a universal assignment requirement:** the first readiness audit appears to have over-weighted final-state correctness and passing tests. Operational demonstrations, explicit knowledge-gap classification and independent checks are reasonable ways to reduce that blind spot. The assessment does not prove this causal explanation or assign score gains to individual fixes. Fresh source collection for every new run, linked-run recovery and a particular capture tool were Project D procedures; future assignments determine whether they apply.

## Discovery and authoring record

The parent [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) points future agents working under `/Users/user/fellowship/` to this file. The existing `CLAUDE.md` points to those instructions. If a tool does not load parent instructions, name `/Users/user/fellowship/PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md` explicitly in the next project's kickoff. For projects elsewhere, pass the path explicitly and follow that repository's own rules. This shared assignment guide is not an installed skill or the plugin's client-engagement playbook; no client sign-off structure is imposed.

Skills actually used to author this guide: **brainstorming** applied the learner's complete brief without redundant discovery questions; **apprentice-workspace:workspace-help** inspected the live catalogue, manifests and filing rules read-only; **apprentice-workspace:writing-for-agents** shaped completion criteria, concise procedures and the discovery pointer. This is an authoring record, not a mandatory skill list for every future task. No plugin library was modified.
---
name: brainstorming
description: "You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation)."
---

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
