A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.
An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.
Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.
PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.
When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. The office raises it to the Clinical Director, who decides whether the application is discontinued. The office does not discontinue an application. The office raises it on what has been verified at the export date: while nothing yet verified supports any requested group, the question stands with the Clinical Director, and it is withdrawn without a disposition when a later verification supports the request.
The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. Current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the office (the manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8), and it is one of the elements this procedure does not handle. Whether a group is supported is decided by rules 1 to 6 alone; the current-experience requirement travels with the packet for the committee and never makes a group unsupported.
Whether a supported request should be granted is not settled here. That is the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff's recommendation and the Governing Body's decision.# Project playbook

Reusable guidance for the learner and agents preparing future assignments. Read at kickoff, after material source changes, and before acceptance or submission. Use the [kickoff checklist](#kickoff-checklist) and [submission checklist](#submission-checklist) as short gates.

These are the learner's standing workflow preferences, adapted to each assignment. Read the actual requirements first; identify any conflict rather than silently changing a required procedure. Currency, units, clocks, authorities, stages, tools, exports and submission structure are project inputs. The Project D examples below are historical cases, not defaults for another project. This file is outside Project D's passed submission; preserve passed code, authentic sources and historical evidence unless a change is explicitly authorized.

## 1. Frame the outcome before building

Read the complete assignment, public assessment criteria, repository instructions, authorized source package, complete interview exports and delivery requirements. Inspect the current installed skill catalogue; read and apply only relevant skills, recording what was used and why.

Explain the intended user, operational outcome, scope, authority boundaries, required deliverable format and observable completion conditions. Show a small example of good output before building; label a mock or proposed layout clearly. Confirm the assignment's clock, date semantics, numeric precision, rounding, units and meaning of missing values. Separate confirmed requirements, assumptions, missing definitions and learner-owned decisions.

Maintain one compact requirement-to-evidence map in an existing project document where practical. Link material public requirements to exact sources, implementation or procedure, and observable evidence. Update gaps as work proceeds; a coverage claim is not proof.

| Requirement / exact source and revision | Implementation or procedure | Observable verification / output | State / gap owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<public requirement; locator>` | `<path or action>` | `<actual result; evidence path>` | `<demonstrated, pending or blocked; owner>` |

**Ready to build:** the outcome and output example are clear, material decisions are identified, and unsupported assumptions are separated from authorized work. Ask about a material unresolved choice; keep routine and independent work moving.

## 2. Establish sufficient business knowledge

Check whether the interview and native sources establish responsibilities, authority, deadlines, exceptions, corrections, partial responses, escalation and completion conditions. For each real gap, identify the missing fact, source/revision, affected behavior, alternative interpretations, consequence, owner and next action. Distinguish absent records, missing definitions, inaccessible sources and learner decisions.

Raise prioritized topics for clarification. Do not repeat an answered topic, prescribe an interview count, or infer a missing business rule. Follow the assignment's interview restrictions. Where interviews or judgment must be learner-led, identify gaps without composing the learner's questions, answers, reasons, approvals or conversations. Preserve authentic exports in the required location and retain their history; the assignment determines session/export rules.

**Ready for the affected branch:** its governing knowledge is supported, or the branch remains explicitly unresolved under a permitted disposition. An unsent draft is not evidence of an escalation or reply.

## 3. Demonstrate the required operational lifecycle

Choose the applicable paths from intake, review, human decisions, execution, reconciliation, corrections, cancellation, partial response, recovery and closure. Mark a path inapplicable only with a reason grounded in scope. Demonstrate required behavior through actual commands or interactions, including real stop/wait/resume boundaries when required. Reconstructing final states does not alone demonstrate those transitions.

Where staged inputs or persisted state apply, verify future-information isolation, stable identities, preserved snapshots, replay behavior and missing/corrupt-state handling.

Separate the evidence provider, reviewer, approver and next action owner. A returning reviewer need not supply the missing evidence. Bind actions and decisions to the applicable subject, revision, actor and source. Reassess affected approvals and obligations when material facts change; preserve prior decisions and execution history.

Check real dependencies through shared evidence, available resources or budget, authority and obligations. Continue independent work where its prerequisites permit it. A shared reviewer or source file alone does not establish a dependency. Resolve only the facts a partial response proves; leave the other issues open. A factual repair supplies no additional approval or execution authority.

**Demonstrated:** primary records show the required transitions and their intermediate states. A complete handoff may contain owned unresolved cases where allowed; their status must remain distinct from approved, executed, paid or closed work.

## 4. Cross-check results independently

Use actual supplied records as primary demonstrations. Label synthetic fixtures and hypothetical recovery probes supplemental, with their purpose and limits. Independently derive important expected results from authorized sources; comparing two outputs from the same implementation is insufficient by itself.

Inspect the actual final reports, files, screens and exports in their required form. Check amounts or quantities, identities, revisions, decisions, statuses, obligations, owners, missing information and next actions across outputs. Use focused regression checks after meaningful changes and an applicable end-to-end check before acceptance. Repeat broader checks when changes, failures or unresolved risk justify them.

**Verified:** each material requirement has an observed result and evidence that supports its scope. Record unrun checks and limitations explicitly. A successful command, schema check, test count or commit count does not establish requirement coverage.

## 5. Diagnose failure and prove recovery

Preserve the failing command or interaction, inputs, source revision, output and error. Establish the cause before changing behavior or rerunning blindly. Make a targeted correction and show a focused before/after result, followed by relevant regression checks. If a prior issue becomes resolved, require evidence for that specific issue and retain its history; unrelated issues remain independent.

Follow the project's documented recovery contract. Preserve damaged or sealed evidence; use a distinct linked reconstruction when required. Other projects may permit a different auditable recovery procedure. Repeated execution must not duplicate actions, obligations or results. Distinguish genuine operational failures from deliberately altered isolated test fixtures. Never manufacture a historical failure or success to improve a score or portfolio.

**Recovered:** observed evidence proves the identified failure is addressed and required history, boundaries and independent work remain correct.

## 6. Preserve source truth and human authority

Retain source precision, identities, provenance and history. Preserve unknown information explicitly and distinguish it from a known zero or a negative decision according to the domain contract. Reconcile conflicting sources through their established authority; do not silently override a written rule with an ambiguous statement.

Only authorized people or supplied scenario records establish approvals, exceptions and real-world actions such as payments. A definition, reply or balanced total is not automatically an authorization or proof of closure. Use the actual completion conditions.

Respect access and confidentiality rules for exports, publication and capture. Never expose credentials, protected interview prompts or restricted trainer answers; use authorized source material rather than hidden grading answers. Authentic required interview submissions follow the assignment's approved access rules. Keep restricted content out of shared reusable guidance.

## 7. Make learner participation meaningful

Use **framing** to explain the target, boundaries and quality standard; **cross-checking** to review actual evidence independently; and **resilience** to diagnose genuine failures and verify recovery. These are practices demonstrated through real work, not activity metrics.

At meaningful decisions, present the relevant source evidence, options, recommendation, reason and constraints. Record the learner's actual choice in the project's existing convention. Keep assumptions labeled. Before acceptance, show the real deliverable and a short review guide: what to inspect, what could be wrong and which judgment is needed. Distinguish “shown” from “inspected” and “accepted”; allow genuine feedback and never invent it.

Proceed with authorized routine implementation without repeated approval requests. Pause dependent work for a required missing decision or authority. Stop optional polishing when acceptance criteria are met.

## 8. Keep capture, readiness and submission traceable

Where capture is required, verify it early through an actual transcript and checkpoint, not configuration alone. Check relevant root and delegated-session payloads when applicable. Report unavailable content, redaction and accounting limitations accurately. Use supported recovery; never fabricate transcripts, lifecycle events or completeness flags.

Before submission, freeze the candidate and verify its exact version or full commit ID, required authentic exports, artifact/run/report paths, capture references and remote synchronization where required. Inspect the committed or exported bytes, not only the working copy. Review what publication exposes and obtain authorization when needed. Remote publication does not itself submit an assignment.

Give a concise readiness account: demonstrated requirements and evidence; unresolved cases with source/revision, missing fact, owner and next action; whether their unresolved disposition is allowed; implementation or verification gaps; and remaining learner actions. Report **implementation complete**, **published**, **submitted** and **graded** as separate facts. Claim submission, inspection or grading only from observed evidence or explicitly attributed learner confirmation.

## 9. Use resources proportionately

Choose tools and models with sufficient capability for the complexity, risk, privacy needs and budget. Explain meaningful cost, latency or reliability tradeoffs. Prefer bounded source reads, focused checks and existing conventions; use additional review or specialist tools where they resolve a material uncertainty. Avoid redundant broad scans and tests, unnecessary artifacts and repeated approval requests. Optimize for reliable outcomes and useful evidence, not token volume, session counts, commits or artificial demonstrations.

## Kickoff checklist

- [ ] Complete assignment, public criteria, instructions, authorized sources and delivery requirements read; relevant skills selected.
- [ ] Intended user, outcome, scope, authority, format and good-output example explained; clock and numeric conventions confirmed.
- [ ] Requirements separated from assumptions, missing knowledge and learner decisions; consequences and owners identified.
- [ ] Compact evidence map and applicable operational paths chosen, including necessary waiting, partial response and recovery behavior.
- [ ] Learner-led interview/decision restrictions and source/capture privacy requirements respected; required capture actually verified.
- [ ] Authorized work, material decision points and a proportionate implementation/verification approach are clear.

## Submission checklist

- [ ] Material changes verified with focused checks; applicable lifecycle and end-to-end acceptance demonstrated using primary records.
- [ ] Important results independently cross-checked; actual deliverables inspected and mutually consistent.
- [ ] Learner shown the real candidate and review guide; actual decisions/feedback distinguished from pending inspection or acceptance.
- [ ] Unresolved cases have sources, owners, next actions and a supported disposition; unfinished implementation and unrun checks are separate.
- [ ] Required original exports, provenance, confidentiality and historical preservation checked against this assignment's rules.
- [ ] Exact candidate/version, required paths, genuine capture and remote synchronization verified; readiness and remaining learner actions stated. Publication, submission and grading statuses are explicit.

## Project D case notes — do not generalize these rules

**Learner-confirmed outcome, recorded 2026-10-18:** first assessment 79.1/100, 68/86 checkpoints; second assessment **96.5/100, 83/86**, rounded to **97** on Passport. Individual checkpoint wording remains private. These scores do not identify which change earned which points or reveal the three remaining checkpoints. No passing score is guaranteed by this playbook.

| Project D-specific fact or rule | Transferable lesson |
|---|---|
| Four arrival batches required separate stopping, waiting and continuation; four reconstructed snapshots alone were insufficient operational evidence | Demonstrate the actual lifecycle and boundaries required by the next assignment |
| Project D used its fixed 2026-11-15 Europe/Amsterdam case clock, integer EUR cents, per-line decimal half-up rounding, null unknown amounts and explicit known zero | Derive numeric, date and missing-value semantics from each project's sources |
| The directory/policy defined Project D's actors, review routes and financial authority; its interview/export and submission formats were assignment-specific | Identify the next project's authorities and deliverables afresh |
| A supplemental late-transfer refund/resolution probe proved the specific issue could clear; actual C18 still lacked that recovery evidence and stayed held | Keep hypothetical recovery separate from actual case evidence; resolve only the issue proved |
| C09's employee supplied revised trip evidence while its returning reviewer retained review authority | Route repairs by responsibility rather than copying the returning reviewer as owner |
| Damaged-state recovery required a distinct linked run preserving the original | Use the governing recovery contract and retain auditable history |
| Actual C20's refund resolved overpayment in batch 3; the separate Finance requirement remained open until batch 4 | Demonstrate partial resolution and remaining conditions in intermediate states |
| The learner's authentic follow-up classified entertainment as personal under written policy; C117 became EUR40 and still awaited its claim approvals | Obtain missing business knowledge and distinguish a supported definition from a claim decision |

The inspected repository HEAD preserved when writing this guidance was `92b9f1c0bba744e06a3ee7b83476ba95aa6ee8d1`. This records the Git baseline; it does not independently establish private grading metadata. Consult the preserved [technical before/after evidence](travel-expense-claim/artifacts/runs/revision-20261018T003113Z/verification/report.md) and [final clarification/verification evidence](travel-expense-claim/artifacts/runs/clarification-20261018T054954Z/verification/report.md). Do not modify those sealed artifacts to fit a later account.

**Inference, not a universal assignment requirement:** the first readiness audit appears to have over-weighted final-state correctness and passing tests. Operational demonstrations, explicit knowledge-gap classification and independent checks are reasonable ways to reduce that blind spot. The assessment does not prove this causal explanation or assign score gains to individual fixes. Fresh source collection for every new run, linked-run recovery and a particular capture tool were Project D procedures; future assignments determine whether they apply.

## Discovery and authoring record

The parent [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) points future agents working under `/Users/user/fellowship/` to this file. The existing `CLAUDE.md` points to those instructions. If a tool does not load parent instructions, name `/Users/user/fellowship/PROJECT_PLAYBOOK.md` explicitly in the next project's kickoff. For projects elsewhere, pass the path explicitly and follow that repository's own rules. This shared assignment guide is not an installed skill or the plugin's client-engagement playbook; no client sign-off structure is imposed.

Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
Accepted sources by element — who may attest
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Table version LARK-ATT-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
The manual we adopted leaves its source lists open. Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends "etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications", and element 5 ends "or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications".
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied the same way twice, so ours is closed. This table is the whole list. A reply from a source on it is admissible. A reply from any source not on it is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional — it is not quietly accepted, and it is not quietly treated as a secondary source.
Two rules cut across every row, both the manual's, both from Section 6, Subsection 1:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
So the applicant is never an accepted source for any element, on any row below, however genuine the document they carry. The reply is filed as received and the request stays open.
Education and training
Class
Accepted sources
Primary source
The degree-granting school's registrar's office or dean's office. The sponsoring institution's graduate medical education office or programme director, for a residency or fellowship
Designated equivalent source
Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG). Federation Credentials Verification Service of the Federation of State Medical Boards (FCVS). American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. National Student Clearinghouse
Secondary source — only on impossibility
The applicant's most recent affiliation's medical staff office, stating how it obtained its own verification, when the school or programme has closed and no designated equivalent source holds the record. The reason is written into the file
Not accepted
The applicant. An alumni association. A departmental colleague writing in a personal capacity. A recruiter, staffing agency or locum tenens agency. A photocopied or scanned certificate from any hand
Licensure
Class
Accepted sources
Primary source
The issuing state licensing board, through its own online verification service or a written reply from the board
Designated equivalent source
Federation of State Medical Boards Physician Data Center
Secondary source
None. A state licensing board does not close
Not accepted
The applicant. A prior employer's copy of a licence. An aggregator or directory not named above
Board certification
Class
Accepted sources
Primary source
The issuing certifying board, through its own verification service or a written reply
Designated equivalent source
American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) certification verification. CertiFACTS. American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. American Board of Physician Specialties (ABPS). American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA)
Secondary source
None
Not accepted
The applicant. A certificate image. A specialty society membership roster
Affiliations and employment
Class
Accepted sources
Primary source
The affiliated hospital's medical staff office. The employer's human resources department or the practice's authorized administrator
Designated equivalent source
A credentials verification organization retained by that affiliation or employer, where the reply names the organization and the affiliation it acted for
Secondary source — only on impossibility
Where the employer has dissolved and no successor holds the records, a written account from the applicant's most recent surviving affiliation of what that affiliation verified, with the reason written into the file
Not accepted
The applicant. A supervisor writing from a personal address without the employer's authority. A professional networking profile. A letter of recommendation offered in place of a dates-and-position verification
What to do with a reply that is not on this table
Record it as received, with who sent it and how it arrived. Nothing is discarded.
Mark the entry still outstanding. An inadmissible reply does not resolve anything.
Keep requesting from a source that is on the table, and keep logging each attempt.
Raise it to the Medical Services Professional, who decides whether the case is one of the impossibility routes above.
Non-response is not impossibility. A source that exists and does not answer is a non-responsive source: it stays outstanding, the attempts keep being logged, and the manual's red flag applies. Only a source that no longer exists opens the secondary route.Code
Question
PPQ-1
Has any licence or registration you hold or have held ever been denied, suspended, revoked, restricted, placed on probation, made subject to a monitoring agreement, surrendered, or subjected to any other action by a licensing board?
PPQ-2
Have your clinical privileges at any institution ever been denied, reduced, restricted, suspended, revoked, not renewed, or made subject to conditions?
PPQ-3
Have you ever resigned from, or withdrawn an application to, a medical staff or training programme while an investigation was pending or in exchange for not conducting an investigation?
PPQ-4
Has any board certification you hold or have held ever been revoked, suspended, or not renewed for cause?
PPQ-5
Have you ever been the subject of a professional review action reportable to a national data bank?
PPQ-6
Have you ever been excluded, debarred or suspended from participation in a federal or state health care programme?
PPQ-7
Have you ever been convicted of, or pleaded guilty or no contest to, a criminal offence other than a minor traffic violation?
PPQ-8
Is there any physical or mental condition, or any use of a substance, that currently impairs your ability to perform the privileges you are requesting, with or without accommodation?
A Yes to any of these is a high-risk finding. It is not by itself a bar to appointment. It is routed to the Clinical Director and presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence.
If a verification the office receives shows that a Yes was owed and a No was given, the office will contact you to confirm the answer before the file goes any further.
Section J — Attestation
I attest that everything in this application is complete, current and correct. I understand that the burden of supplying verifiable information is mine, and that a discrepancy between what I have declared and what a source reports will be put back to me in writing.
Signature and date.
What the office does with a completed form
The office records receipt, screens the nine completeness conditions in the procedure, and either takes the file up or writes to you with the missing items. It then writes to the schools, programmes, boards, employers, affiliations and referees named above. It does not use anything you hand over yourself in place of their replies.Professional peer reference — blank request and return form
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-REF-2026.1.
The office sends this form directly to the referee the applicant named, and the referee returns it directly to the office. A form that reaches us through the applicant cannot be used.
Part 1 — completed by the Medical Staff Office before sending
Field
Content
Referee identifier
The office's identifier for this referee on this file
Applicant
Name and degree
Privileges requested
The privilege groups on the application
Request date
The date this request was sent
Request number
1, 2 or 3 — each reminder is a fresh numbered request
We write up to three times, 21 calendar days apart. If no reply has reached us by the 64th day after the first request, we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open. We do not close it as satisfied and we do not count it.
Part 2 — completed by the referee
Field
What to enter
Are you a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant?
Tick Yes or No. This box is never left blank
Relationship
How you worked with the applicant, in your own words
Your specialty
The clinical discipline you practise, chosen from the same list the applicant chose from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery — or your own discipline if it is not on that list
Dates you worked directly together
First and last date. Leave the last date blank only if you still work together
Recommendation
Recommend without reservation, Recommend, Recommend with reservations, or Do not recommend
Comments
Character, clinical experience, competency, and anything else you want on the record
Signature and signature date
The date you sign. This is the date we measure currency from — not the date we receive the form
Who may give a peer reference
Three conditions, each independent, all three required:
you have worked directly with the applicant within the two years ending on the day you sign this form;
you practise in the same clinical discipline as the applicant;
you are not a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant.
If any one of the three does not hold, say so on the form and return it anyway. We will record your reply, and we will not count it towards the two references the appointment needs. That is not a judgment about you or about the applicant; it is the rule we apply to every file the same way.
Currency
A reference is current if the signature date is within two years of the date the file is presented to the Governing Body. A reference signed a long time before the file is presented stops being current, and we ask again.
Part 3 — completed by the Medical Staff Office on return
Field
Content
Received date
The date the completed form reached the office
How it arrived
Secure portal, letter, fax or email, direct from the referee
Nothing in Part 2 is edited, summarized or corrected by the office. What the referee wrote is what goes in the file, including a relationship or a specialty that differs from what the applicant told us.

The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
Accepted sources by element — who may attest
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Table version LARK-ATT-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
The manual we adopted leaves its source lists open. Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends "etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications", and element 5 ends "or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications".
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied the same way twice, so ours is closed. This table is the whole list. A reply from a source on it is admissible. A reply from any source not on it is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional — it is not quietly accepted, and it is not quietly treated as a secondary source.
Two rules cut across every row, both the manual's, both from Section 6, Subsection 1:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
So the applicant is never an accepted source for any element, on any row below, however genuine the document they carry. The reply is filed as received and the request stays open.

Record it as received, with who sent it and how it arrived. Nothing is discarded.

def request_history(tables, as_of, contract):
    groups = indexed(tables["verification-attempts.csv"], "application_id", "element", "subject_ref")
    replies = defaultdict(list)
    for name, identity, element in [("verification-replies.csv", "entry_id", None),
                                    ("certification-replies.csv", "declaration_id", "board-certification"),
                                    ("peer-reference-replies.csv", "referee_id", "peer-reference")]:
        for o in tables[name]:
            row = o["row"]
            replies[(row["application_id"], element or row["element"], row[identity])].append(o)
    referees = indexed(tables["peer-referees.csv"], "application_id", "referee_id")
    result = []
    for (app, element, subject), occurrences in sorted(groups.items()):
        ordered = sorted(occurrences, key=lambda o: (o["row"]["attempt_date"], o["source"]["batch"], o["source"]["csv_row"]))
        dates = [date.fromisoformat(o["row"]["attempt_date"]) if o["row"]["attempt_date"] else None for o in ordered]
        observed = replies.get((app, element, subject), [])
        request = {"application_id": app, "element": element, "subject_ref": subject,
                   "attempts": occurrences, "recorded_attempt_count": len(occurrences),
                   "attempt_intervals_days": [(b - a).days if a and b else None for a, b in zip(dates, dates[1:])],
                   "observed_reply_occurrences": observed,
                   "reply_observed": bool(observed), "reply_qualifies": "not-evaluated",
                   "request_satisfied": "not-evaluated", "no_response_is_verification": False}
        if element == "peer-reference":
            anchors = {o["row"]["first_request_date"] for o in referees.get((app, subject), [])}
            anchor = next(iter(anchors)) if len(anchors) == 1 and "" not in anchors else None
            # A first-request/attempt disagreement is not silently repaired.
            if anchor and dates and dates[0] and anchor != dates[0].isoformat():
                anchor = None
            request["peer_first_request_date"] = anchor
            request["peer_first_request_sources"] = referees.get((app, subject), [])
            request["peer_scheduled_dates"] = (
                [(date.fromisoformat(anchor) + timedelta(days=n * contract["attempt_spacing_days"])).isoformat()
                 for n in range(3)] if anchor else None)
            overdue = date.fromisoformat(anchor) + timedelta(days=contract["peer_overdue_offset_days"]) if anchor else None
            request["peer_day64_date"] = overdue.isoformat() if overdue else None
            request["no_returned_row_at_day64"] = as_of >= overdue.isoformat() and not observed if overdue else None
            request["limits"] = "Schedule arithmetic only; no qualifying-reference count, notice sent, fourth reminder, element hold or closure inferred"
        result.append(request)
    return result


def decision_history(tables, documents, policy):
    index = indexed(tables["correspondence.csv"], "application_id")
    apps = indexed(tables["applications.csv"], "application_id")
    result = []
    ids = set()
    for document in documents:
        if not document["source"]["path"].startswith("decisions/"):
            continue
        fields = metadata(document["text"])
        checks = authority_checks(fields, policy)
        identifier = fields["Decision ID"]
        if identifier in ids:
            raise GroundworkError("review_identity", "Duplicate decision identifier; preserve source occurrences and investigate")
        ids.add(identifier)
        receipt = [o for o in index.get((fields["Application"],), [])
                   if o["row"]["document_path"] == document["source"]["path"]
                   and o["source"]["batch"] == document["source"]["batch"]]
        if len(receipt) != 1:
            raise GroundworkError("document_index", "Decision lacks a unique matching correspondence entry")
        known = [o for o in apps.get((fields["Application"],), [])
                 if o["source"]["batch"] <= document["source"]["batch"]
                 and o["row"]["received_date"] and o["row"]["received_date"] <= fields["Decision date"]]
        at_decision = latest_applications(known).get(fields["Application"]) if known else None
        matches = fields["Revision"] == at_decision["row"]["revision"] if at_decision else None
        failed = checks["first_failed_authority_check"]
        if failed is None and matches is False:
            failed = "applicant/revision"
        result.append({"decision_id": identifier, "source": document["source"],
                       "document_sha256": digest(document["text"].encode()), "recorded_fields": fields,
                       "receipt": receipt[0], "authority_checks": checks,
                       "recorded_revision_at_decision_date": at_decision["row"]["revision"] if at_decision else None,
                       "revision_source": at_decision["source"] if at_decision else None,
                       "first_failed_independent_condition": failed,
                       "admitted": False if failed else None,
                       "reason": failed if failed else "Prior presentable packet and packet-revision match unproved: G1/G2",
                       "not_evaluated": ["packet identity/presentability before decision", "outcome/reason", "supersession"],
                       "activation": "not-evaluated"})
    # Receipt date and source row preserve the supplied received ordering, not filename order.
    return sorted(result, key=lambda d: (d["source"]["batch"], d["receipt"]["row"]["date"], d["receipt"]["source"]["csv_row"]))

                        key = v["row"][identity]
                        if not key or key in found:
                            raise GroundworkError("review_identity", "Ambiguous restated-row identity")
                        found[key] = v
                    return found
                current = version_map(row["revision"])
                old = version_map(previous["row"]["revision"]) if previous else {}
                item["restated_comparisons"][name] = {
                    "identity_column": identity,
                    "added": [{"id": k, **current[k]} for k in sorted(current.keys() - old.keys())],
                    "removed": [{"id": k, **old[k]} for k in sorted(old.keys() - current.keys())],
                    "changed": [{"id": k, "before_source": old[k]["source"], "after_source": current[k]["source"],
                                 "fields": differences(old[k]["row"], current[k]["row"], ("revision",))}
                                for k in sorted(current.keys() & old.keys())
                                if differences(old[k]["row"], current[k]["row"], ("revision",))],
                    "unchanged_ids": [k for k in sorted(current.keys() & old.keys())
                                      if not differences(old[k]["row"], current[k]["row"], ("revision",))],
                }
            item["evidence_reuse_conclusion"] = "not-evaluated"
            item["CV_reconciliation"] = "not-evaluated:G2"
            previous, prior_revision = o, rev
            result.append({"application_id": app, **item})
    return result


def request_history(tables, as_of, contract):
    groups = indexed(tables["verification-attempts.csv"], "application_id", "element", "subject_ref")
    replies = defaultdict(list)
    for name, identity, element in [("verification-replies.csv", "entry_id", None),
                                    ("certification-replies.csv", "declaration_id", "board-certification"),
                                    ("peer-reference-replies.csv", "referee_id", "peer-reference")]:
        for o in tables[name]:
            row = o["row"]
            replies[(row["application_id"], element or row["element"], row[identity])].append(o)
    referees = indexed(tables["peer-referees.csv"], "application_id", "referee_id")
    result = []
    for (app, element, subject), occurrences in sorted(groups.items()):
        ordered = sorted(occurrences, key=lambda o: (o["row"]["attempt_date"], o["source"]["batch"], o["source"]["csv_row"]))
        dates = [date.fromisoformat(o["row"]["attempt_date"]) if o["row"]["attempt_date"] else None for o in ordered]
        observed = replies.get((app, element, subject), [])
        request = {"application_id": app, "element": element, "subject_ref": subject,
                   "attempts": occurrences, "recorded_attempt_count": len(occurrences),
                   "attempt_intervals_days": [(b - a).days if a and b else None for a, b in zip(dates, dates[1:])],
                   "observed_reply_occurrences": observed,
                   "reply_observed": bool(observed), "reply_qualifies": "not-evaluated",
                   "request_satisfied": "not-evaluated", "no_response_is_verification": False}
        if element == "peer-reference":
            anchors = {o["row"]["first_request_date"] for o in referees.get((app, subject), [])}
            anchor = next(iter(anchors)) if len(anchors) == 1 and "" not in anchors else None
            # A first-request/attempt disagreement is not silently repaired.
            if anchor and dates and dates[0] and anchor != dates[0].isoformat():
                anchor = None
            request["peer_first_request_date"] = anchor
            request["peer_first_request_sources"] = referees.get((app, subject), [])
            request["peer_scheduled_dates"] = (
                [(date.fromisoformat(anchor) + timedelta(days=n * contract["attempt_spacing_days"])).isoformat()
                 for n in range(3)] if anchor else None)
            overdue = date.fromisoformat(anchor) + timedelta(days=contract["peer_overdue_offset_days"]) if anchor else None
            request["peer_day64_date"] = overdue.isoformat() if overdue else None
            request["no_returned_row_at_day64"] = as_of >= overdue.isoformat() and not observed if overdue else None
            request["limits"] = "Schedule arithmetic only; no qualifying-reference count, notice sent, fourth reminder, element hold or closure inferred"
        result.append(request)
    return result


def decision_history(tables, documents, policy):
    index = indexed(tables["correspondence.csv"], "application_id")
    apps = indexed(tables["applications.csv"], "application_id")
    result = []
    ids = set()
    for document in documents:
        if not document["source"]["path"].startswith("decisions/"):
            continue
        fields = metadata(document["text"])
        checks = authority_checks(fields, policy)
        identifier = fields["Decision ID"]
        if identifier in ids:
            raise GroundworkError("review_identity", "Duplicate decision identifier; preserve source occurrences and investigate")
        ids.add(identifier)
        receipt = [o for o in index.get((fields["Application"],), [])
                   if o["row"]["document_path"] == document["source"]["path"]
                   and o["source"]["batch"] == document["source"]["batch"]]
        if len(receipt) != 1:
            raise GroundworkError("document_index", "Decision lacks a unique matching correspondence entry")
        known = [o for o in apps.get((fields["Application"],), [])
                 if o["source"]["batch"] <= document["source"]["batch"]
                 and o["row"]["received_date"] and o["row"]["received_date"] <= fields["Decision date"]]
        at_decision = latest_applications(known).get(fields["Application"]) if known else None
        matches = fields["Revision"] == at_decision["row"]["revision"] if at_decision else None
        failed = checks["first_failed_authority_check"]
        if failed is None and matches is False:
            failed = "applicant/revision"
        result.append({"decision_id": identifier, "source": document["source"],
                       "document_sha256": digest(document["text"].encode()), "recorded_fields": fields,
                       "receipt": receipt[0], "authority_checks": checks,
                       "recorded_revision_at_decision_date": at_decision["row"]["revision"] if at_decision else None,
                       "revision_source": at_decision["source"] if at_decision else None,
                       "first_failed_independent_condition": failed,
                       "admitted": False if failed else None,
                       "reason": failed if failed else "Prior presentable packet and packet-revision match unproved: G1/G2",
                       "not_evaluated": ["packet identity/presentability before decision", "outcome/reason", "supersession"],
                       "activation": "not-evaluated"})
    # Receipt date and source row preserve the supplied received ordering, not filename order.
    return sorted(result, key=lambda d: (d["source"]["batch"], d["receipt"]["row"]["date"], d["receipt"]["source"]["csv_row"]))


def timeline(store, state_sha, rules_path, rules_sha):
    history = store.at(state_sha)
    manifest = history["state"]["manifest"]

+"""Immutable internal workflow results, separate from evidence and schema snapshots."""
+
+import os
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from .validation import GroundworkError, confined_file, digest, json_bytes, read_json
+
+
+class WorkflowStore:
+    def __init__(self, root):
+        if root.is_symlink():raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "Workflow store cannot be symlinked")
+        self.root = root.resolve()
+
+    def at(self, sha):
+        if not isinstance(sha,str) or len(sha) != 64 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in sha):
+            raise GroundworkError("workflow_hash", "Invalid workflow occurrence hash")
+        raw = confined_file(self.root, "objects/"+sha+".json").read_bytes()
+        if digest(raw) != sha:raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Workflow result differs from its content hash")
+        value = read_json(raw)
+        if value.get("format") != "credentialing-workflow/1":raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Unknown workflow format")
+        return value
+
+    def current(self):
+        path = self.root / "HEAD.json"
+        if path.is_symlink() or (self.root/"objects").is_symlink():raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "Symlinked workflow objects/HEAD")
+        if not path.exists():
+            if (self.root/"objects").exists() and any((self.root/"objects").iterdir()):
+                raise GroundworkError("workflow_missing_head", "Preserve workflow objects without HEAD; do not initialize over them")
+            return None
+        head = read_json(path.read_bytes());sha = head["sha256"];result = self.at(sha)
+        seen = {sha};cursor = result
+        while cursor["previous_workflow_sha256"]:
+            before = cursor["previous_workflow_sha256"]
+            if before in seen:raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Workflow predecessor cycle")
+            seen.add(before);prior = self.at(before)
+            if prior["batch"]+1 != cursor["batch"] or prior["as_of"] > cursor["as_of"]:
+                raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Workflow sequence/clock regressed")
+            cursor = prior
+        if cursor["batch"] != 1:raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Workflow chain does not start at batch one")
+        return sha,result
+
+    def predecessor(self, batch, state_sha, explicit):
+        current = self.current()
+        if current and current[1]["batch"] == batch:
+            if current[1]["evidence_state_sha256"] != state_sha or current[1]["previous_workflow_sha256"] != explicit:
+                raise GroundworkError("workflow_predecessor", "Changed rerun input; preserve current workflow and reconstruct separately")
+            return self.at(explicit) if explicit else None
+        if batch != (current[1]["batch"]+1 if current else 1) or explicit != (current[0] if current else None):
+            raise GroundworkError("workflow_predecessor", "Supply exact current workflow predecessor and next batch")
+        return current[1] if current else None
+
+    def commit(self, report):
+        self.root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

+        try:fd = os.open(lock,os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY,0o600)

+                if current[0] != sha:raise GroundworkError("workflow_changed", "Changed retained result; use separate reconstruction, never overwrite")
+                return sha,"unchanged"
+            objects = self.root/"objects";objects.mkdir(exist_ok=True);path = objects/(sha+".json")
+            if path.exists():
+                if path.is_symlink() or path.read_bytes()!=raw:raise GroundworkError("workflow_corrupt", "Existing workflow object differs")
+            else:
+                with path.open("xb") as out:out.write(raw);out.flush();os.fsync(out.fileno())
+            descriptor,name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".head-",dir=self.root)

+            return sha,"stored"

"""Integrate immutable workflow reports with the guarded schema writer."""

from pathlib import Path

from .storage import Store
from .validation import GroundworkError, digest, json_bytes, read_json, schema_validate
from .workflow import process
from .workflow_store import WorkflowStore
from .writer import SnapshotWriter, snapshot_path


def process_run(evidence_store, state, work_store, previous, rules, rules_sha, root, schema_path):
    if root.is_symlink():raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "Output root cannot be a symlink")
    root = root.resolve(strict=True)
    evidence = Store(evidence_store);retained = evidence.at(state);batch = retained["state"]["manifest"]["batch"]
    workflow = WorkflowStore(work_store);prior = workflow.predecessor(batch,state,previous)
    report = process(evidence,state,rules,rules_sha,prior,previous)
    schema = read_json(schema_path.read_bytes())
    for app in report["applications"]:
        if app["schema_application"] is not None:
            schema_validate(app["schema_application"],{"$schema":schema["$schema"],"$defs":schema["$defs"],"$ref":"#/$defs/application"})
    run_sha,change = workflow.commit(report)
    folder = root/"deliverables/workflow"
    if any(p.is_symlink() for p in [folder,*folder.parents]):raise GroundworkError("unsafe_path", "Symlinked report output")
    folder.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);name=f"deliverables/workflow/batch-{batch:02}-{run_sha}.json";path = root/name
    raw = json_bytes(report)
    if path.exists():
        if path.is_symlink() or path.read_bytes()!=raw:raise GroundworkError("changed_report", "Preserve existing report, do not overwrite differing bytes")
    else:
        with path.open("xb") as out:out.write(raw)
    receipt = {"operation":"process", "workflow_result":change, "workflow_sha256":run_sha,
               "previous_workflow_sha256":previous, "batch":batch,"as_of":report["as_of"],"report":name,
               "summary":report["summary"],"assessed_snapshot_written":False,
               "schema_projection_conflicts":report["schema_projection_conflicts"]}
    if report["schema_projection_conflicts"]:
        receipt["assessment_result"] = "blocked-at-schema-projection"
        return receipt,3
    if batch>1 and not (root/snapshot_path(batch-1)).exists():
        receipt["assessment_result"] = "blocked-missing-assessed-predecessor"
        return receipt,3
    candidate = {"schema_version":"credentialing-snapshot/1","snapshot_id":f"workflow-{batch:02}-{run_sha[:24]}",
                 "predecessor":None,"batch":batch,"as_of":report["as_of"],
                 "consumed":{"record_files":[f["path"] for f in report["source_manifest"]["files"] if f["kind"]=="records"],
                             "documents":[f["path"] for f in report["source_manifest"]["files"] if f["kind"]=="document"]},
                 "produced":[snapshot_path(batch)],"rules_file":"deliverables/rules.md",
                 "applications":[a["schema_application"] for a in report["applications"]]}
    output = SnapshotWriter(root,schema).publish([candidate],{batch:report["as_of"]},[])
    receipt.update(assessment_result="schema-snapshot-generated-or-unchanged",snapshot=output,
                   assessed_snapshot_written=output["result"]=="written", existing_snapshot_retained=output["result"]=="unchanged",
                   business_outcomes="Only source-supported or explicitly labeled synthetic facts; Git sealing separate")
    return receipt,0

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import date,timedelta
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);parser.add_argument('--inputs',type=Path,required=True);parser.add_argument('--reports',type=Path,required=True);args=parser.parse_args()
    index=json.loads((args.reports/'current.json').read_text());all_rows={};results=[]
    for batch in (1,2,3):
        folder=args.inputs/f'batch-{batch:02}';manifest=json.loads((folder/'input.manifest.json').read_text());clock=manifest['as_of']
        for name in ('applications.csv','peer-referees.csv','peer-reference-replies.csv','declared-history.csv','verification-replies.csv'):
            with (folder/name).open(newline='') as stream:all_rows.setdefault(name,[]).extend(csv.DictReader(stream))
        report_path=Path(index[str(batch)]);report=json.loads(report_path.read_text());assert report['as_of']==clock
        apps={}
        for row in all_rows['applications.csv']:
            if row['application_id'] not in apps or int(row['revision'])>int(apps[row['application_id']]['revision']):apps[row['application_id']]=row
        checks=[]
        for case in report['applications']:
            app=apps[case['application_id']];assert int(app['revision'])==case['revision']
            named={r['referee_id'] for r in all_rows['peer-referees.csv'] if r['application_id']==app['application_id'] and int(r['revision'])<=int(app['revision'])}
            assert case['intake']['conditions']['7_two_named_referees']==(len(named)>=2)
            latest={}
            for r in all_rows['peer-reference-replies.csv']:
                if r['application_id']==app['application_id'] and (r['referee_id'] not in latest or r['received_date']>latest[r['referee_id']]['received_date']):latest[r['referee_id']]=r
            count=0
            for r in latest.values():
                signed=date.fromisoformat(r['signature_date']);last=date.fromisoformat(r['last_worked_together_end']) if r['last_worked_together_end'] else signed
                # These source dates have no leap-day ambiguity; fail rather than clamp one.
                recent=signed.replace(year=signed.year-2)<=last<=signed
                current=signed<=date.fromisoformat(clock)<=signed.replace(year=signed.year+2)
                direct="We worked in the same department and I supervised several of the applicant's cases."==r['relationship_stated']
                count+=bool(r['related_or_partner']=='No' and r['referee_specialty_stated']==app['discipline'] and recent and current and direct and app['first_received_date']<=r['received_date']<=clock)
            assert count==case['elements']['references']['detail']['qualifying_distinct_referees'],app['application_id']
            history=[r for r in all_rows['declared-history.csv'] if (r['application_id'],r['revision'])==(app['application_id'],app['revision'])]
            school={r['to_date'] for r in history if r['entry_type']=='medical-school'};assert len(school)==1
            start=date.fromisoformat(next(iter(school))).toordinal()+1;end=date.fromisoformat(clock).toordinal();uncovered=set(range(start,end+1))
            for r in history:
                lower=date.fromisoformat(r['from_date']).toordinal();upper=date.fromisoformat(r['to_date'] or clock).toordinal();uncovered.difference_update(range(max(start,lower),min(end,upper)+1))
            segments=[]
            for n in sorted(uncovered):
                if not segments or n!=segments[-1][-1]+1:segments.append([])
                segments[-1].append(n)
            gaps=[{'from':date.fromordinal(s[0]).isoformat(),'to':date.fromordinal(s[-1]).isoformat(),'days':len(s)} for s in segments if len(s)>=30]
            assert gaps==[{k:g[k] for k in ('from','to','days')} for g in case['elements']['gaps']['detail']['gaps']]
            checks.append({'application_id':app['application_id'],'revision':case['revision'],'named_referees':len(named),'qualifying_current_returned_fields':count,'declared_gaps':gaps})
        notice=folder/'letters/2026-02-18_missing-items_APP-2026-019.md'
        if batch==1:
            assert notice.exists() and '2026-03-20' in notice.read_text();due=(date(2026,2,18)+timedelta(days=30)).isoformat();assert due=='2026-03-20'
        case19=next(c for c in report['applications'] if c['application_id']=='APP-2026-019');assert case19['status']==('intake-incomplete' if batch==1 else 'ineligible-clock-expired')
        results.append({'batch':batch,'report':str(report_path),'report_sha256':hashlib.sha256(report_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'checks':checks,'actual_missing_item_due':'2026-03-20','status_APP019':case19['status']})
    print(json.dumps({'method':'Original CSVs and actual letter; daily set subtraction, distinct incremental referee IDs and calendar arithmetic; no product imports','results':results,'limits':'Checks these quantities and clocks, not complete intake, accreditation, CV reconciliation or clinical authority'},indent=2))

| Result | Meaning in this implementation |
|---|---|
| Established actual result | Supported by current exported rows/documents and the named rule. A known necessary failure can establish false readiness despite unrelated unknowns |
| Missing-evidence result | Null only in the internal report, with its dependency/owner/action; never silently converted into an assessment enum or boolean |

accreditation and secondary-route authorization. It requires dated retained

an explanation clinically or discontinue a file. No observation is invented for

review before being treated as established actual facts.


`deliverables/synthetic/workflow-demo/`, with invented source batches, review
records, decisions, receipts, three nested snapshots and proof. Its stages are
packet-presentable → approved-not-yet-effective → active-with-conditions. The

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m credentialing verify-snapshot --root deliverables/synthetic/workflow-demo --path deliverables/snapshots/batch-03.json --schema snapshot.schema.json
```

outputs are retained, not relabeled as current full-workflow results.

Source and workflow stores reject skipped/corrupt/missing predecessors, orphaned
state without HEAD, symlinked destinations and changed retained batches/results.

are present locally. Full actual schema snapshots remain absent with precise
per-field reasons. G1/G2 and scoped source issues are human work, not a reason to

push or Classroom submission is performed. The learner owns actual choices and
final review; put any choice/reason early in a turn (first 600 characters).

name: practitioner-credentialing
description: Process Larkhollow initial-appointment export batches with persisted evidence, scoped human review, owned queues, chronological decisions and guarded credentialing snapshots.
---

# Practitioner credentialing

Run from this repository root using [README](README.md). This Skill implements
the dated workflow and writer. A usable implementation does not imply that its
supplied applicants have enough evidence for complete assessment snapshots.

## One batch and exact predecessor

1. Read the [rules register](deliverables/rules.md), original schema and current
   [source audit](docs/readiness-audit.md). Use one authorized physical batch
   manifest, its export date, pinned rules and the exact preceding state hashes.
2. If needed, materialize only the reviewed manifest's batch using the README
   preparer outside business runtime. `stage` retains original bytes; it is not
   a completeness pass. Never load the combined archive into a batch runner.
3. Invoke `process` with evidence store/state, separate work store, pinned
   element rules/hash and `--previous-workflow` for later batches. README supplies
   exact three-batch commands. Batch 3 must resume batch 2. Do not replace missing
   or corrupt predecessors with an empty run.
4. Read stdout's workflow hash/report and assessment result. Exit 3 can mean the
   workflow report was retained while its schema projection is blocked; it is
   not an approved business deferral. Continue independent work from that exact
   workflow receipt. Exit 2 requires failure investigation. Exit 0 means a
   generated/unchanged schema result, not acceptance or submission readiness.

## Evidence and authority

Preserve raw sources, original outcomes, refused records, revision bindings,
request attempts and prior workflow objects. Re-evaluate changed entry fields,
current licence/peer dates and affected elements; unrelated checks continue.
Retain readiness and disposition history when an element reopens or a file ends.

Separate established results, missing evidence and synthetic assumptions. A known
false necessary condition may disprove readiness independently of another
unknown. Missing signature/CV evidence is neither an applicant omission nor a
pass. G1/G2 remain MSP-owned human review tasks with due null absent a record.
Do not invent a written notice, clock, source class, age threshold or approval.

Five judgments remain human: gap explanation adequacy; disqualifying finding;
eligibility discontinuation; appointment/privilege recommendation; and GB
approval/modification/deferral/denial. Check actual people, bodies, terms and
protocol against the roster. A role asserted in a record is not its authority.
Record the actual disposition; never write the learner's choice or reasoning.

For evidence absent from CSVs, use only genuine source-linked human records
conforming to [the MSP observation protocol](docs/human-observation-protocol.md).
The adapter permits factual checks and MSP source-route determination, not
reserved clinical judgments. It validates dated source references and roster
identity, not cryptographic authorship. No actual review record is fabricated.
Return to the learner before newly supplied evidence/conventions are adopted.

## Outputs and schema boundary

`deliverables/workflow/current.json` selects full actual-case workflow reports;
immutable object hashes link their predecessors. Reports contain six element
results, exact dependencies, source observations, owned queues, decisions,
activation/condition records and history. Null means unknown only in this
internal format. Use the unchanged schema's application definition where its
meanings are established. Never substitute a new enum or nullable boolean in a
required snapshot.

Only a fully representable caseload and assessed predecessor chain can generate
`deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json`. Otherwise retain the full report and exact
unmet fields. No application is omitted to force a batch through. Partial needs
an actual schema-valid snapshot; deferred needs an admitted GB business hold.

`deliverables/synthetic/workflow-demo/` contains the separate invented SYNTH-only
end-to-end package. Its source assumptions/positive results do not establish
facts for supplied applicants. Mixed synthetic/actual application inputs are

# Practitioner credentialing

Run from this repository root using [README](README.md). This Skill implements
the dated workflow and writer. A usable implementation does not imply that its
supplied applicants have enough evidence for complete assessment snapshots.

## One batch and exact predecessor

1. Read the [rules register](deliverables/rules.md), original schema and current
   [source audit](docs/readiness-audit.md). Use one authorized physical batch
   manifest, its export date, pinned rules and the exact preceding state hashes.
2. If needed, materialize only the reviewed manifest's batch using the README

   a completeness pass. Never load the combined archive into a batch runner.
3. Invoke `process` with evidence store/state, separate work store, pinned
   element rules/hash and `--previous-workflow` for later batches. README supplies
   exact three-batch commands. Batch 3 must resume batch 2. Do not replace missing
   or corrupt predecessors with an empty run.
4. Read stdout's workflow hash/report and assessment result. Exit 3 can mean the
   workflow report was retained while its schema projection is blocked; it is
   not an approved business deferral. Continue independent work from that exact
   workflow receipt. Exit 2 requires failure investigation. Exit 0 means a
   generated/unchanged schema result, not acceptance or submission readiness.

## Evidence and authority

Preserve raw sources, original outcomes, refused records, revision bindings,
request attempts and prior workflow objects. Re-evaluate changed entry fields,
current licence/peer dates and affected elements; unrelated checks continue.
Retain readiness and disposition history when an element reopens or a file ends.

Separate established results, missing evidence and synthetic assumptions. A known
false necessary condition may disprove readiness independently of another
unknown. Missing signature/CV evidence is neither an applicant omission nor a
pass. G1/G2 remain MSP-owned human review tasks with due null absent a record.
Do not invent a written notice, clock, source class, age threshold or approval.

Five judgments remain human: gap explanation adequacy; disqualifying finding;
eligibility discontinuation; appointment/privilege recommendation; and GB
approval/modification/deferral/denial. Check actual people, bodies, terms and
protocol against the roster. A role asserted in a record is not its authority.
Record the actual disposition; never write the learner's choice or reasoning.

For evidence absent from CSVs, use only genuine source-linked human records
conforming to [the MSP observation protocol](docs/human-observation-protocol.md).
The adapter permits factual checks and MSP source-route determination, not
reserved clinical judgments. It validates dated source references and roster
identity, not cryptographic authorship. No actual review record is fabricated.
Return to the learner before newly supplied evidence/conventions are adopted.

## Outputs and schema boundary

`deliverables/workflow/current.json` selects full actual-case workflow reports;
immutable object hashes link their predecessors. Reports contain six element
results, exact dependencies, source observations, owned queues, decisions,
activation/condition records and history. Null means unknown only in this
internal format. Use the unchanged schema's application definition where its
meanings are established. Never substitute a new enum or nullable boolean in a
required snapshot.

Only a fully representable caseload and assessed predecessor chain can generate
`deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json`. Otherwise retain the full report and exact
unmet fields. No application is omitted to force a batch through. Partial needs
an actual schema-valid snapshot; deferred needs an admitted GB business hold.

end-to-end package. Its source assumptions/positive results do not establish
facts for supplied applicants. Mixed synthetic/actual application inputs are
rejected. Lower-level historical reports remain under evidence/assessments.
